relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with SSADH deficiency and a homozygous ALDH5A1 variant: "Whole‐exome sequencing revealed a previously unreported homozygous variant in the ALDH5A1 gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and copied each span verbatim from the paper (tolerating Unicode hyphens and no-break spaces), and checked every span occurs in the paper. In scope: the single patient (label 'patient', rule 5) and her two parents, who are described ('The mother is a healthy 27-year-old primigravida, and the father is a healthy 32-year-old') and tested ('Both parents were heterozygous carriers for this variant.'); labels 'mother of patient' and 'father of patient' (rule 2). The 182 patients of Attri et al and the 450 literature patients are mentioned only at group level and get no rows. Inheritance for the patient's homozygous variant is recorded as 'inherited unspecified parent' because both parents are stated carriers and the enum has no value for biparental inheritance. Variant type not stated by the authors (not derived from HGVS). Pathogenicity: authors classify the variant as VUS (class 3) under ACMG yet argue for pathogenicity from biochemistry, MRS and structural modelling; no ACMG codes printed. The parents' rows carry the VUS classification because that sentence names this exact variant. Age at SSADH diagnosis is not stated (only age 7 months for the hypothyroidism diagnosis), so age_at_diagnosis is not reported. Checklist: 'she does not have seizure disorders, dystonia, or movement disorders' was used to exclude seizures, dystonia, exertional dyskinesia and hemiballismus (the latter two as movement disorders); ataxia left not reported. 'Says a few words but no sentences' at 3 years and speech therapy were not taken as an explicit speech impairment (recorded only as a phenotypic feature); global developmental delay was not taken as intellectual disability. Normal findings were recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27; the normal eye examination and unremarkable systemic examination are recorded as written (whole examinations, nothing more specific excluded). Table 1 values (e.g. prolactin 771 vs 102-496) that the text does not call abnormal were not recorded as features. Table 1 and Table 2 have time points, not patients, as columns. Possible inconsistencies in the paper: the Discussion says 'high levels of serum and urinary GABA on thyroid hormone supplementation' but Table 1 reports urine GHB, not urine GABA; the Discussion says MRS demonstrated 'accumulation of GHB and GABA in the brain' while the Results describe only GABA; the hypothyroidism diagnosis is dated 7 months while the Table 1 column is '8 mo old'; Figure 5 gives PDB 2W8R while the text gives 2W8O. No stacked cells.
